events: net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.ComputeFovModifierEvent (GAME bus, Dist.CLIENT — static @SubscribeEvent method StaticFovClientEvents.onComputeFovModifier, attached by @EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT, bus = EventBusSubscriber.Bus.GAME), not by the module's onInitialize; default priority NORMAL; clamps getNewFovModifier() down to 1.0f, leaves values below 1.0 alone)
notes:
SIZE: the entire module is two files, 71 lines total — StaticFovModule.java (31 lines) and client/StaticFovClientEvents.java (40 lines), both verified with wc -l. There is nothing else: no mixins (grep for "fov" in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json and mixin/ returns nothing), no data files, no lang keys (grep "fov"/"static" over assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/*.json returns nothing), no assets, no commands, no items/blocks/entities (no DeferredRegister anywhere in the module).

HOW IT WORKS (the whole logic): StaticFovClientEvents.onComputeFovModifier does `if (event.getNewFovModifier() > 1.0f) event.setNewFovModifier(1.0f);` (lines 59-61). That's it. Values below 1.0 pass through untouched, so FOV-narrowing effects (bow draw zoom) keep working. The clamp target 1.0f is HARDCODED — there is no config key to soften it or to pick a different ceiling. static_fov is the only place in src/ that touches FOV at all (grep "Fov" over src/main/java hits nothing outside this module except the bundle import/registration lines).

CONFIG: the module passes `AbstractModuleConfig::createDefault` → `AbstractModuleConfig.DefaultModuleConfig` (core/AbstractModuleConfig.java:198-208), which does not override buildModuleSpecificConfig. So the config section has ONLY the two universal keys built by AbstractModuleConfig.buildConfig: `enabled` (default = module.isEnabledByDefault()) and `debug_logging` (enum AUTO/ON/OFF, default AUTO). configKeys is genuinely empty. NOTE: unlike other modules there is no generated-config proof file — test-server/config/vanillaplusadditions-common.toml was last written 2026-07-03, i.e. four days BEFORE this module existed, so its absence there means nothing.

DEBUG LOGGING IS INERT HERE: neither of the two module files contains a single logger call, and nothing in core/ consumes AbstractModuleConfig.shouldDebugLog()/isDebugLoggingEnabled() generically — each module calls it for itself. So setting `debug_logging = ON` for static_fov produces no output. The only log lines that ever name this module are the inherited lifecycle messages in AbstractModule ("Initializing module: {}" :94, "Module initialized: {}" :104), and those are plain slf4j debug/info, unaffected by the module's debug_logging key.

enabledByDefault=true comes from the interface default `Module.isEnabledByDefault()` (core/Module.java:73-75); StaticFovModule overrides neither it nor shouldInitialize() (AbstractModule.shouldInitialize() returns true, core/AbstractModule.java:112-114).

SURPRISING COUPLING — the module's own onInitialize() is deliberately EMPTY (StaticFovModule.java:27-30, with a comment saying so). The event handler is wired by `@EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT, bus = EventBusSubscriber.Bus.GAME)`, i.e. NeoForge's annotation scan attaches it at mod load, completely bypassing the module lifecycle. Consequences a doc writer should know: (1) the handler is always attached on a client even while the module is disabled — it re-checks `module.isModuleEnabled()` on every single FOV computation instead; (2) because the check is per-event, a change to `enabled` is picked up without a restart or world reload.

ENABLED-CHECK CHAIN (relevant to "how do I turn it off"): AbstractModule.isModuleEnabled() (:202-215) first returns true when `isInitialized()` is false, and isInitialized() is merely `modEventBus != null` (:168-170), which initialize() sets as its first statement — so after mod construction the check always reads the real value. It then calls ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled(moduleId, config.isEnabled()) (core/ModuleManager.java:205-208), which lets a runtime override from `/vpa module enable|disable|clear <id>` (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:239-266, 397, 423) win over the config file. Caveat: the clamp reads the CLIENT JVM's ModuleManager. In singleplayer client and integrated server share one JVM, so the command reaches it; against a dedicated server the command only flips the server-side ModuleManager and cannot change what a remote client's camera does.

DEFENSIVE NO-OP: getModule() looks the module up by string id ("static_fov") via ModuleManager and returns null if it is missing or of another type; the handler then silently does nothing. So in a build where the module is not registered, the client code is inert rather than crashing.

NO STANDALONE JAR: static_fov does NOT appear in build.gradle's `standaloneModules` list (checked over the full list, build.gradle:386-465). There is no `vpa_static_fov` jar — the feature ships only inside the bundle jar.

NO DOCS PAGE YET: there is no docs/modules/static_fov.md; grep -i "fov" over the whole docs/ tree returns nothing. Outside code, the only prose that exists is README.md:175-176 and the CHANGELOG entry.

README CONTRADICTION: README.md:176 says the FOV stops widening for "sprinting, Speed, elytra/flight". The class javadoc (StaticFovModule.java:9-11) instead names "sprinting, Speed effects, creative flight, Soul Speed", and the client-class javadoc a third list ("sprinting, Speed effect, creative flight"). None of the three is provable from this repository — the code does not enumerate causes at all, it just clamps whatever value arrives at ComputeFovModifierEvent (NeoForge's hook around the vanilla player FOV modifier). Anything that changes the view angle OUTSIDE that event is untouched by this module. Whether elytra flight or Soul Speed actually route through that event cannot be decided from this repo, so the README's "elytra" claim should be re-checked in game before it is repeated in new documentation.

NO TODO/FIXME comments in either file. No dead code.

oneLiner: Your view stays at the same zoom level when you sprint, drink a Speed potion or fly in creative, instead of the camera pulling back every time you speed up — while zoom-in effects like drawing a bow still work normally.
shortDescription: Stops the FOV from widening when the player moves faster (sprint, speed, flight).
